correctness_confidence.basis: I re-derived by hand: the Gaussian-moment limit 1/8 in Thm 3, Lemma 4/5 and Prop 6 (Cesaro test, remainder bound), and the explicit n>=10^4 arithmetic in (12) (e.g. -9/4+42/19=-3/76; 1/2-10/21=1/42). All consistent. Thm 2, Lemma 10, Thm 11 and the Mathieu uniformity step are terse and I only checked them for plausibility, not line by line.

rigor.basis: Finite certificate (Lemmas 4-5, Prop 6) and the explicit constant are clean and checkable. Sections 2 and 6 and the proof of Thm 11 compress key steps into 'uniformly bounded', 'by compactness', 'a polynomial times a Gaussian dominates'; the Mathieu expansion uniformity over the window n/2+c rests on cited asymptotics. Quantifiers are mostly explicit; non-effectivity of M_A, C_A, N_A is honestly stated.

novelty.basis: Removes the log n factor from the exponent of the cited Tan-Wang-Huang-Chen bound (via a local analytic estimate), gives the sharp 1/sqrt8 circle-root barrier, and a one-interior-zero threshold. Techniques build heavily on [1],[2]. The author discloses that a targeted search did not exhibit these bounds, and that priority is not certified; I did not browse and did not check these references.

significance.basis: Sharpens a quantitative refinement of a known negative answer (Erdos 973, per [2]) and gives a clean dichotomy: circle roots give a constant barrier, one interior root collapses it. Niche subject; gaps between the disk lower bound exp(-C sqrt n) and the superalgebraic upper bound remain, and the optimal rates are explicitly left open.

reproducibility.basis: The explicit constants (n>=10^4) and the one-root parameter formulas can be verified by hand, and I checked part of them. The paper cites supplementary symbolic/numerical audits (Gaussian-rational Newton identities, 34 degree classes), but they are not in the PDF, so I could not inspect or run them. Theorem 2 relies on a non-explicit implicit-function construction.

summary: The manuscript studies the minimal normalized residual ||P'-lambda P||_2/||P||_2 over degree-n polynomials with zeros in the closed disk. It proves (i) a sharp limit 1/sqrt8 when all zeros are on the circle, via a Mathieu ground-state bound plus an explicit family; (ii) a lower bound exp(-C sqrt n) for every C>sqrt((8/3)log17), with explicit exp(-3 sqrt n) for n>=10^4, from a finite certificate refining Tan-Wang-Huang-Chen [1]; (iii) superalgebraic upper bounds with a fixed number of interior zeros at distance ~n^(-1/3), and collapse with exactly one interior zero (rate O(n^(-1/6))); (iv) a polynomial lower barrier if the root radius is fixed below 1. The finite-certificate chain and constants I recomputed hold. The asymptotic constructions (Sections 2, 6, 11) are argued compactly and I only checked them for plausibility. Claims of priority are properly hedged. External citations (arXiv 2026 items, Erdos 973) were not looked up by me.
strengths: Clear scope statements: what is not claimed (optimal rates, finite extremizers, constants optimality) is listed in Sections 1 and 8.
Finite certificate (Prop 6) is transparent and the explicit n>=10^4 constants check out in my hand recomputation.
Sharp dichotomy between all-circle zeros (constant barrier 1/sqrt8) and one interior zero (vanishing residual), with an exact zero-count threshold.
Explicit parameter formulas for the one-interior-zero family (cubic (18), circle-parameter solution) make that part of the construction checkable.
Candid disclosure of AI assistance and of the limits of the verification and priority search.
weaknesses: Proofs of Theorem 3 (upper bound), Lemma 10 and Theorem 2 are summary-level; several uniformity claims (secondary maximum bound for H_c(s), Jacobian/IFT neighbourhoods, outer-arc estimates) are asserted without displayed computations.
The supplementary computations cited in Section 8 are not part of the artifact and cannot be assessed from the PDF.
The superalgebraic upper bound is non-effective (no bounds on M_A, C_A, N_A) and leaves a large gap to the exp(-C sqrt n) lower bound; the optimal rates remain open.
Novelty relative to [1] and [2] depends on arXiv items I did not consult; the improvement is a log-factor removal plus an arbitrary slope.
Theorem 3's lower-bound step relies on uniform Mathieu asymptotics over a growing window, cited from DLMF and not re-proved.
potential_errors: Mathieu uniformity: the expansion E(L) = -L + sqrt(L/2) - 1/16 + O(L^(-1/2)) must hold with a uniform remainder for L=(n+1)lambda over the whole minimizing window; the paper asserts this but I did not verify it.
Lemma 10 proof (rational conical combination, kernel vector strictly positive) is sketched; a non-degeneracy or full-rank detail could fail for particular node choices.
Theorem 11: uniformity over the 34 residue classes k, and the claim that the discriminant and denominators stay positive with a_n, c_n in (-1,1), are stated rather than shown.
Remark 7 gives a general sufficient condition C^2>2log(1+2/s)/(1-2s) without proof beyond 'same proof'; I did not rederive it (s=1/8 gives C0^2=(8/3)log17 and is consistent).
Section 6: the 'unique global maximum / modulus gap' claim for the perturbed degree-6 factor is argued by local curvature plus compactness, not by explicit computation.
strong_novelty_candidates: The sharp circle-root constant 1/sqrt8 for the global residual, through the Mathieu ground state.
The exact zero-count threshold: no collapse with zero interior zeros, collapse with exactly one, residual O(n^(-1/6)).
Removing the log factor in the sqrt(n) exponent of the Tan-Wang-Huang-Chen lower bound, for an arbitrary scalar slope.
